Definition: from σέλας (brilliancy; probably akin to the alternate of G138, through the idea of attractiveness); the moon:--moon.
BiblicalUsage: Selene is the moon, and Paul sets it among the glories: there is one glory of the sun, and another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars. And Peter, quoting Joel, says the moon shall be turned into blood, before that great and notable day of the Lord come.
TheologicalSignificance: The moon has its own glory now, and a darker sign to come, for the lights of heaven are God's to dim.
